# Abstract {.unnumbered}

::: {.content-hidden when-format="pdf"}
## The Journey from Consumer to Investor: Designing a Financial AI Companion for Young Adults to Help With Sustainable Consumption
:::

The emerging field of *planetary health* recognizes profound interconnections between our economic behaviors, ecosystem services (water, air, soil), the climate crisis, and human health. How we use money to interact with companies, through shopping, saving, and investing, impacts the life-supporting biosphere we depend on. From an ecological perspective, financial choices can either support more environmentally responsible companies or sustain polluters.

In Taiwan, college students report strong environmental values, yet, consistent with the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB), attitudes alone are not enough. My thesis investigates how AI assistants could empower individual college students to hold companies accountable by leveraging transparency-focused Digital Product Passports (DPPs) with data-driven benchmarks (reinforcing social norms) and sustainability facts at the moment of choice (a sense of control).

In my inquiry, I leveraged design research to find design concepts for *simple AI-based generative user interfaces* to help young adults engage in *sustainable financial actions*. Throughout the process, I conducted a survey of over 900 students from 21 universities across Taiwan, in-person user testing with 30 participants, and 7 expert interviews. The major contribution of the study is an interactive AI-companion prototype.

Keywords: Human-AI Interaction, Digital Sustainability, Transparency
